# measure <img src="man/figures/logo.png" align="right" height="139" alt="measure hex logo" />

<!-- badges: start -->
[![Lifecycle: experimental](https://img.shields.io/badge/lifecycle-experimental-orange.svg)](https://lifecycle.r-lib.org/articles/stages.html#experimental)
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/JamesHWade/measure/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/JamesHWade/measure/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
[![Codecov test coverage](https://codecov.io/gh/JamesHWade/measure/graph/badge.svg)](https://app.codecov.io/gh/JamesHWade/measure)
<!-- badges: end -->

measure brings analytical instrument data (spectroscopy, chromatography, mass spectrometry, and other curve-based measurements) into [tidymodels](https://www.tidymodels.org/).

Instead of preprocessing spectra in ad-hoc scripts before modeling, you add `step_measure_*()` steps to a [recipes](https://recipes.tidymodels.org/) pipeline. Parameters learned from the training set stay inside resampling splits, tunable steps work directly with [tune](https://tune.tidymodels.org/), and the output comes back as an ordinary data frame for modeling or reporting.

## Installation

Install the development version from GitHub:

```r
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("JamesHWade/measure")
```

## Example

The built-in `meats_long` dataset contains 215 near-infrared (NIR) spectra of meat samples paired with measured water, fat, and protein content (the signal column is named `transmittance` for compatibility with `modeldata::meats`, though the values are absorbance).

```{r example, message = FALSE}
library(measure)
library(recipes)

data(meats_long)
head(meats_long)
```

Convert the long-format curves into measure's internal representation, take a smoothed first derivative, apply Standard Normal Variate (SNV) scaling, and pivot the processed curves back to wide predictor columns:

```{r recipe}
rec <- recipe(water + fat + protein ~ ., data = meats_long) |>
  update_role(id, new_role = "id") |>
  step_measure_input_long(transmittance, location = vars(channel)) |>
  step_measure_derivative_gap(gap = 3, segment = 3) |>
  step_measure_snv() |>
  step_measure_output_wide(prefix = "nir_")

prepped <- prep(rec)
processed <- bake(prepped, new_data = NULL)
processed[1:5, 1:8]
```

Stopping before `step_measure_output_wide()` keeps each processed spectrum in the `.measures` list column, which makes it easy to inspect how the pipeline changed the curves:

```{r visualization, message = FALSE, fig.width = 7.5, fig.height = 5.2, fig.cap = "Ten NIR spectra from meats_long before and after a gap first derivative and SNV scaling.", fig.alt = "Two stacked line plots of spectrometer channel versus signal for ten meat samples. The top panel shows raw absorbance curves with broad baseline offsets; the bottom panel shows the gap first derivatives after SNV scaling, centered around zero with sharper spectral features."}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

rec_viz <- recipe(water + fat + protein ~ ., data = meats_long) |>
  update_role(id, new_role = "id") |>
  step_measure_input_long(transmittance, location = vars(channel)) |>
  step_measure_derivative_gap(gap = 3, segment = 3) |>
  step_measure_snv()

processed_long <- bake(prep(rec_viz), new_data = NULL)

sample_ids <- unique(meats_long$id)[1:10]

raw_plot <- meats_long |>
  filter(id %in% sample_ids) |>
  transmute(
    sample_id = id,
    location = channel,
    value = transmittance,
    stage = "Raw absorbance"
  )

processed_plot <- processed_long |>
  filter(id %in% sample_ids) |>
  transmute(sample_id = id, .measures) |>
  unnest(.measures) |>
  mutate(stage = "Gap 1st derivative + SNV")

plot_data <- bind_rows(raw_plot, processed_plot) |>
  mutate(
    stage = factor(
      stage,
      levels = c("Raw absorbance", "Gap 1st derivative + SNV")
    )
  )

ggplot(plot_data, aes(location, value, group = sample_id)) +
  geom_line(colour = "#0072B2", alpha = 0.55, linewidth = 0.4) +
  facet_wrap(vars(stage), ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Spectrometer channel", y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )
```

## What's in the package

measure includes over 100 recipe steps and analysis functions. The [function reference](https://jameshwade.github.io/measure/dev/reference/index.html) lists everything; here is how the package is organized:

- Signal preprocessing: baseline correction (ALS, polynomial, SNIP, rolling ball, airPLS, arPLS, morphological), smoothing and derivatives (moving average, Gaussian, median, Savitzky-Golay, wavelet, Fourier, gap derivatives), scatter correction (SNV, MSC, EMSC, OSC), sample normalization, variable scaling, region trimming and resampling, and chromatogram alignment (shift, DTW, PTW, COW).
- Peaks and features: peak detection, integration, filtering, and deconvolution (`step_measure_peaks_*()`), plus region integrals, peak ratios, moments, and binning.
- Calibration, QC, and method validation: weighted calibration curves (`measure_calibration_fit()`), single-analyte LC/GC batch quantitation (`measure_quantify_batch()`), drift and batch correction, LOD/LOQ, precision and accuracy, Bland-Altman, Deming and Passing-Bablok regression, ISO GUM uncertainty budgets, control charts, and ICH Q2 / bioanalytical acceptance criteria.
- Structured records and multi-dimensional signals: `measure_record()`, `measure_acquisition()`, and n-dimensional measurement tables for keeping raw 1D curves, 2D arrays (such as LC-DAD or EEM), and ragged MS scans tied to sample metadata and source files, along with JCAMP-DX import and export.

## Practice datasets

The package ships with small datasets for examples and testing:

| Dataset | Technique | Samples | Description |
|---------|-----------|---------|-------------|
| `meats_long` | NIR | 215 | Meat composition spectra (long format of `modeldata::meats`) |
| `bioreactors_small` / `bioreactors_large` | Raman | 210 / 42 | Bioreactor glucose monitoring (`data(glucose_bioreactors)`) |
| `hplc_chromatograms` | HPLC-UV | 20 | Simulated chromatograms with five compounds |
| `sec_chromatograms` / `sec_calibration` | SEC/GPC | 10 / 5 | Simulated polymer chromatograms and MW standards |
| `maldi_spectra` | MALDI-TOF | 16 | Simulated mass spectra across four groups |

## Companion tools and related packages

- [measure.sec](https://jameshwade.github.io/measure.sec/) adds SEC/GPC detector processing and molecular-weight distribution calculations through measure's technique pack registry.
- [measure-service](https://jameshwade.github.io/measure-service/) exposes measure and measure.sec workflows over MCP for automated and assistant-driven lab pipelines.
- The [Python package](https://github.com/JamesHWade/measure/tree/main/python) in this repository implements SNV, MSC, and Savitzky-Golay steps for `mlfeatures`.

If you work with spectral data in R outside tidymodels, [prospectr](https://github.com/l-ramirez-lopez/prospectr), [ChemoSpec](https://bryanhanson.github.io/ChemoSpec/), and [mdatools](https://mdatools.com/) are also worth a look.
